THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

These appeals, filed by the claimant and the Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, challenge the judgment and award dated December 23, 2017, issued in MVC No.
291/2016 by the learned Principal Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Hassan.
2. The claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident on October 25, 2015.
The accident occurred when the rider of the offending motorcycle, riding rashly and negligently, collided with the claimant as he was crossing the road.

The Tribunal, after considering the evidence on record,
awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,45,320/- with interest at 6% per annum.
The claimant has appealed for an enhancement of the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal, while the Insurance Company has appealed to challenge the liability to pay the compensation amount.
3. The learned counsel for both parties has been heard.
4. The claimant, who was 29 years old at the time of the accident on October 25, 2015, sustained multiple injuries.
These included a mild head injury, a laceration on the left tibia with the bone exposed, a fracture of the left tibia, tenderness over the chest, and tenderness in the T1 spine.

The doctor, who was examined as PW2, opined that injuries No. 1 to 3 were grievous NC:
2024:KHC:21055 while the rest were simple in nature.
The claimant underwent treatment involving open reduction and nail and plate fixation.

He was admitted to the hospital on October 25, 2015,
and discharged on October 30, 2015.
PW2 assessed the physical disability of the claimant at 30% for the lower limb and stated that the claimant would need further surgery, which would cost Rs.30,000/-.
5. The Tribunal, noting that the fracture of the claimant's elbow had united, assessed the permanent disability to the whole body at 18%.

The claimant, who is stated to be engaged in agriculture and business, had his notional income assessed at Rs.9,000/- per month, in contrast to the Rs.6,000/-
per month assessed by the Tribunal, due to the lack of proof of income.
6. The Insurance Company argued that the motorcycle involved in the accident was falsely implicated.
Ex. R3, the MLC extract from the Government Hospital in Channarayapatna, indicated that the accident had occurred between the riders of two motorcycles.
The Tribunal noted that the MLC extract did not specify who provided the information when the claimant was admitted to the hospital, and that he was conscious upon admission.

RW2, the author of Ex.R2, stated that the MLC register was written by her trainees and admitted that there was no mention of who provided the information regarding the accident.
RW2 confirmed that the claimant was conscious when admitted, and neither the claimant nor his relatives reported that the accident NC: 2024:KHC:21055 involved two motorcycles.
The police investigation resulted in a charge sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle, with no evidence suggesting the accident involved two motorcycles.
8. After discharge from the government hospital, the claimant continued treatment at Janapriya Hospital.
Ex. P9, another MLC extract, indicated that the claimant's injuries were caused by the accident involving the offending motorcycle.
The claimant consistently maintained that his injuries resulted from the negligent and rash riding of the motorcycle rider.
The cross-examination did not yield any evidence to dispute this claim.

The Tribunal, after thoroughly reviewing the evidence,
concluded that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle rider,
which was covered under the policy issued by the Insurance Company.

Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal requires to be reassessed as follows:

The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,19,480/- as against Rs.3,45,320/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.1,74,160/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till actual realization.
To this extent, the impugned award stands modified.

10. The respondent - Insurance Company to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,74,160/-
